components.name: Layer Chip
components.description: Timeline layer toggle: the one pill-shaped control, with a square colour swatch.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 28px; padding: 0 8px; margin-right: 4px; border: 1px solid #363636; border-radius: 9999px; background: #292929; color: #e3e3e3; font: 400 12px ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #474747; } .ds-chip[aria-pressed='false'] { background: transparent; color: #919191; } .ds-chip-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; box-sizing: border-box; background: var(--layer); border: 1px solid var(--layer); } .ds-chip[aria-pressed='false'] .ds-chip-dot { background: transparent; } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #6478ff; outline-offset: 1px; }

narrative.overview:
A clean bench beside the running app. The panel is where a Lit developer lays a component out to look at it: its properties, its renders, its parts. The bench itself stays quiet. Surfaces are near-black ink in dark and paper greys in light, separated by hairlines rather than shadows. Colour belongs to what is being inspected (syntax hues for values, layer colours on the timeline) and to the one brand voice, the blue of the Lit flame, which marks what is selected, active or actionable.

It is precise and exact. Corners are square, borders are one pixel, numbers and code are set in a monospace with fixed widths, and every size steps along a fine 2px/4px grid made for dense tooling. Nothing is approximate or decorative; anything that does not help the user read their component is left off the bench.

The system is open to revision. The panel's design system (tokens, `packages/lit-components`, the Web Awesome theme) may change as the panel is redesigned. Rules below marked **(provisional)** describe how the system is today and are under review; unmarked rules are firm.
keyCharacteristics: Quiet ink and paper surfaces; the user's data is the loudest thing on screen.
One brand accent, Lit blue, for selection, focus and primary action.
Square everything, hairline borders, no shadows on resting surfaces.
Mono for data and code, system sans for interface text.
Light and dark are equal, generated from one token source.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Lit blue means "selected, active or yours to act on". It is not decoration, not a heading colour and not a background for areas.

rules.name: The Earned Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every text token clears 4.5:1 on the surfaces it sits on. Where the upstream design system's value fell short, the token was lightened or darkened and the source comment says so. Keep doing that rather than reverting to the upstream value.

rules.name: The Two Schemes Rule
rules.body: Every colour exists in both schemes. A change that only defines or checks one scheme is unfinished.

rules.name: The Mono Means Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks what came from the user's code or runtime (names, values, paths, durations). Interface words such as setting labels and button text stay in the sans.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separate regions with a 1px border or one tonal step, never with a shadow. A shadow means "this is above the page".

dos: **Do** read every colour, size and space from a `--lit-devtools-*` token, and add a token in `packages/webawesome-theme-lit/src/tokens/` when one is missing.
**Do** check every change in light and dark.
**Do** keep text at 4.5:1 or better, and say so in a comment when a token departs from the upstream design system to get there.
**Do** set user data in mono and interface text in sans.
**Do** keep clickable rows at least 24px tall.
donts: **Don't** use Lit blue for decoration, headings or large fills.
**Don't** put a shadow on a resting surface; use a border or a tonal step.
**Don't** round a control, card or panel while the square rule stands; the pill is only for badges, chips and dots.
**Don't** fill an origin tag or metadata label like a button; muted text is enough.
**Don't** let a form or a line of prose run the full width of a wide panel.
